questions.heading: Consequence Is the Cost of One Failure, Added Up From Its Parts
questions.stem: A feeder failure interrupts 3,000 of a utility's 150,000 customers for 4 hours. How much does that one failure add to the utility's SAIDI for the year?

options.text: 0.02 minutes, the number of customers interrupted divided by all customers served
options.says: 3,000 / 150,000 = 0.02 is the SAIFI contribution, interruptions per customer, not minutes.

options.text: 240 minutes, the length of the outage that each interrupted customer went through
options.says: SAIDI divides the customer-minutes by every customer served, not only those interrupted.

options.text: 720,000 minutes, the customer-minutes of the outage before any division at all
options.says: SAIDI is per customer served; the customer-minutes still have to be divided by 150,000.

options.text: 4.8 minutes, the customer-minutes of the outage divided by all customers served

questions.heading: Risk Is the Expected Failure Cost per Year
questions.stem: A substation has a PoF of 4% next year, and one failure costs $5,000k, so its risk is $200k a year. A finance analyst sets aside $200k for this substation's failures next year and says the year is covered. What is wrong?

options.text: Nothing, since an expected cost is the amount that next year will actually cost
options.says: An expected cost is an average over many imagined years; the simulated A006 years each cost 0 or the whole CoF.

options.text: Next year costs either 0 or $5,000k; $200k is the average over many such years
options.says: Right: risk is an expected value, so it says nothing about the spread of a single year.

options.text: The risk is $5,000k, since a failure costs the whole consequence in every year
options.says: The consequence is paid only in a year with a failure, which has a 4% chance.

options.text: The $200k is the most next year can cost, since risk caps the cost of a year
options.says: A year with a failure costs $5,000k, far above the $200k average.

questions.heading: Count Expected Failures When a Failed Asset Is Repaired and Kept
questions.stem: A worn recloser is repaired and put back each time it fails, without being made any younger. Over the coming year its cumulative hazard grows from 2.0 to 3.2. Each failure costs $50k. What is its expected failure cost for the year?

options.text: About $34.9k, from the chance of at least one failure, 1 - e^-1.2, times the cost
options.says: That counts at most one failure; a repaired recloser can fail again, and the expected count is 1.2.

options.text: About $160k, from the cumulative hazard at the year's end, 3.2, times the cost
options.says: The count for the year is the growth of the cumulative hazard over the year, not its value at the end.

options.text: About $60k, from the expected failures in the year, 3.2 - 2.0, times the cost
options.says: Right: expected failures = Lambda(a + 1) - Lambda(a) = 1.2, times $50k.

options.text: About $50k, from one failure times the cost, since a count above one is cut to one
options.says: Only a probability is capped at 1; an expected count of failures can exceed 1, as the worn asset's 1.66 a year shows.
